design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (comp_dependents_claims_and_payments), frozen 2026-10-05 14:05:00 MST. Revision 2 (policy-task audit rework).

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 1: prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [4, 6, 4]: restoration (root) 6, resumption 4, temporary total 4; 2 value_input edges.

[Why a good test] Rafael asks for the money the overturned 2024 PTSD reduction held back. The restoration is not worked out until the award runs again (it is suspended after two returned payments) and is fixed only after a release cites every temporary total decision (the knee's never was). The agent hands the account confirmation to the veteran, releases the temporary total past-due, and restores only from the late Supplemental Claim's receipt (530 days after the notice, past the 365-day lane window, continuing no earlier review) - not from the 2024 reduction (the near-miss, 14115.78).

[Scope ledger] This task: comp_ext_suspension_release (resume_award_release_withheld_86166e35, user), comp_ext_temporary_total_past_due (release_temporary_total_past_due_0acb107c), comp_ext_review_restoration (release_review_restoration_92058ca9). Task 0 holds the other four. Not lit here: replacement (award suspended; afterwards the returned months are paid by the resumption release), dependency release (latest dependency claim 2023, in every payment), decision past-due (the SMC (k) decision of 2026-03-20 left no past-due: effective 2026-03-10, payable from April, April paid with it; the temporary total is outside its list), opening release (award running since 2011).

[Problem tree card] root comp_ext_review_restoration. Edge 1 restoration -> resumption, value_input, gate rr_paid, state form (negated): "A restoration after a reduction overturned on review is not worked out until the award's status is running again." Opening: status suspended; only the resumption sets a suspended award running. Edge 2 restoration -> temporary total, value_input, gate rr_paid, state form (affirmative): "A restoration after a reduction overturned on review is fixed only after the award's payment history carries a past-due release citing every temporary total rating decision on the award." Opening: no retro row cites d7587361-dfdb-43a6-97ce-fb2dbfab988b. Deletion runs: 13995.73 and 8507.27 instead of 2352.63. The prerequisites commute (both orders identical); gold puts the resumption first (inherited base: past-due on a suspended award released only on resumption - F-C1 has no consequence on values).

[Factor card - revision 2]
- resumption (11643.10; all-baseline 5844.96): months method (6985.86); spouse (10872.05); children (11131.75); parents (11024.0).
- temporary total (6154.64; 4928.21): the temporary total rate is now the baseline; SMC (k) months method - SMC (k) effective 2026-03-10 inside the temporary total months -> 1 of 2 (6014.77); spouse (5714.04); children (5862.44); parents (5800.88). Paid is now the monthly payments actually issued for those months (band of issue dates), not the latest gross.
- restoration (2352.63; 0.0): start method (cross-difficulty appeal, multi-source; baseline = the reduced-rate date, reachable for every timely review) 14115.78; 100 percent tier months method (temporary total months falling within the restoration months, 2; tiers: temporary total only / individual unemployability only, dated from its effective date / both, capped / none) 0.0; SMC (k) months method (6 of 10) 1513.41; spouse 678.35; children 1242.27; parents 1008.31.
Stamps: smc_k_count 1 says one award is in effect; the tiers taken rest on its 2026-03-10 effective date (reading the stamp as every month gives 6294.51 for the temporary total and 2912.11 for the restoration). tdiu_granted false matches the ledger and no factor reads it.

[Base-invariant card] Resumption: declared overwrites of the suspension cure and release clauses and the adjust-month clause; temporary total and restoration: declared overwrites of the rating_change past-due clause and the adjust-month clause. All releases policy_scope on comp_retro_payment; no fee agreement, no debt; single signature. Account updated 2026-09-22, thirteen days before today (10-day lead time met, closes T1-O1).

[World rows] customer; award; 5 claims; 7 decisions (PTSD and knee grants, proposal, reduction, SMC (k), temporary total, resumption on the same claim); 3 dependents; 23 monthly payments from August 2024 (the reduced-rate start; closes T1-O3) and 2 returns; review + 2 review actions.

[Standard solution] reads -> hand over resumption 2026-05..2026-09 11643.10 -> temporary total d7587361-dfdb-43a6-97ce-fb2dbfab988b 2026-03..2026-04 6154.64 -> restoration 6b7c198a-1d0b-4d1d-a442-c71ba0d48a61 2025-12..2026-09 2352.63.

[Verification run] _t1_world.py: B 11643.10, T 6154.64, E 2352.63; sensitivities and skips as above; alternative order identical.

[Revision 2 log - audit items] F-A1: incarceration tiers removed. F-A3: the temporary total rate moved into the baseline; the method factor is now the SMC (k) effective-date months. F-A4: restoration start ladder re-cut - baseline is the reduced-rate date (stated in baseline.rule), tiers are late review without continuation (receipt date) and continuation of a late earlier review (that review's receipt date); the scope-restating 'granted' conjunct is gone. F-A6: SMC (k) now effective 2026-03-10, inside both computations' months. F-B6/F-B7: declared overwrites; temporary total 'paid' now reads the payments issued for its months. F-E1/F-E2: as task 0. F-E4: resumption read from the decision on the same claim. F-E5: continuation honoured only within the continuous-pursuit window. T1-O1: account change moved to 2026-09-22. T1-O2: observation kept - the award row and the review record carry the restored 70 percent; no comp decision row is added because an increase-granted row would light the decision past-due. T1-O3: payment ledger extended back to August 2024. Dossier stamp and near-miss sentences corrected.

[Revision 3 log - audit round 2] R2-A2: restoration_full_tier_months re-cut - the temporary total months are counted only where they fall within the restoration months (the whole months to the resumption less those before the start), individual unemployability months run from its effective date (whole months to today less one, capped by the restoration months), a fourth tier covers both; values on this world unchanged (restoration 2352.63; factor baseline 0.0). R2-T1-O1: the decision past-due now applies only when a decision's effective date makes payable a month whose monthly payment was already issued when the decision was made; the 2026-03-20 SMC (k) decision (effective 2026-03-10, first payable month April, paid 2026-05-01 with it) is outside it. R2-O2: the resumption, temporary total and restoration rules now scope out months with an incarceration adjustment. R2-O3: charter-level (the dependency release now includes parents); not lit here.
user_scenario:
You are Rafael T. Quintanilla, a 42-year-old Navy veteran who lives in Tucson, Arizona. You are direct and a little impatient, you use plain words, and you like to get to the point, but you are fair with whoever picks up. Back in 2024 VA cut your PTSD rating from 70 percent to 50 percent. Last November you filed a supplemental claim with new records from your therapist, and in August VA decided it in your favor and put you back at 70 percent. The decision letter said you would be paid what the cut had held back from you, and you still have not seen that money, so you are calling to have it paid to you now. You open by giving your name, Rafael T. Quintanilla, and your phone number, 5205550113, and by saying you want the money VA owes you from your PTSD rating being put back. You are fine with the representative doing whatever VA needs to do on its end to get it out to you; you want it actually paid, not just a figure.

Only when the representative asks you to verify who you are do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 1862, your VA file number, 317409286, and your date of birth, 1984-04-23, each when it is asked for. If you are asked about your bank or your recent deposits, you say your old credit union account was closed early this summer and you put your new checking account, ending in 4417, in online on September 22, and that is where the money should go. If you are asked about your family, you say you are married to Teresa, your son Mateo is twelve, and your father Hector lives with you and depends on you. If you are asked about your knee, you say you had surgery in February and were laid up for a couple of months. If you are asked whether you filed any other appeal on the cut, you say the supplemental claim was the only one. You do not know dollar amounts or month counts, and if you are asked for one you say you would have to go by VA's records.

If the representative tells you that you have to confirm your payment account yourself and hands that step over to you, you do it with exactly the details the representative gives you and read back what the system tells you. If the representative explains that other amounts on your award have to be released first, you tell them to go ahead. When the representative tells you the money the rating cut held back has been released, you say thanks and end the call. You never suggest steps, amounts or an order yourself, and you do not ask for anything beyond that money.
